for: independent humanities/social-science researcher (no institutional affiliation), media & Southeast Asian studies

funders.name: BRIN RIIM Collaboration international co-funding
funders.eligible_who: Researchers from Indonesian universities AND independent research organizations, partnering with counterpart agencies in Japan, China or Malaysia on a joint research project
funders.amount_note: Co-funding for a joint research/innovation project; not a simple conference-travel grant, and exact amounts not confirmed on the page found
funders.cycle: Tied to periodic joint calls with partner-country agencies; no standing conference-travel deadline
funders.requires: A partner institution/agency in Japan, China or Malaysia and a joint project proposal, not just conference attendance
funders.source_note: Explicitly says BRIN's national research/innovation funding (RIIM) is 'open to researchers beyond BRIN, including universities and independent organizations' -- one of the few Indonesian schemes that names independent researchers, but it funds collaborative projects, not simply travel to present a paper

funders.note: LPDP (Indonesia Endowment Fund for Education) is Indonesia's major national funding body, but its programs are degree-scholarships (bachelor's/master's/PhD study abroad) and related study travel, not a scheme an independent, non-enrolled researcher can apply to for conference travel.
Not applicable: this researcher is independent with no university, library or institutional affiliation, so there is no home-institution travel fund to check.

funders.name: The Japan Foundation -- Arts and Culture Small Grant Program
funders.eligible_who: Individuals and organizations in Southeast Asia (including Indonesia) engaged in arts and cultural exchange projects, including documentation and archiving of local culture
funders.amount_note: Small grant tier; exact amount not confirmed on the page found
funders.cycle: Annual call, 2026 fiscal year program open; exact 2026 deadline not confirmed on the page found
funders.requires: A cultural-exchange or arts project proposal (not simply conference attendance); typically an application through the relevant Japan Foundation office
funders.source_note: Real, active regional (Japan-Southeast Asia) cultural funder; a plausible fit for archiving/documentation work but not conference travel specifically

funders.name: Kelola Foundation (Yayasan Kelola) -- Hibah Seni (Arts Grants)
funders.eligible_who: Indonesian arts practitioners and communities (music, dance, theatre, visual arts) working on production, documentation or touring projects
funders.amount_note: Amount not confirmed on the page found; historically funds production costs, documentation, and sometimes travel related to performances/exhibitions
funders.cycle: Periodic open calls; exact 2026 cycle dates not confirmed on the page found
funders.requires: An arts/documentation project proposal; independent practitioners are eligible
funders.source_note: Indonesia's own long-running (est. 1999) national arts foundation -- the closest domestic fit for an independent archivist of Indonesian popular music and zines, though it funds projects/documentation rather than travel to a specific conference

funders.note: No destination-specific scheme was found for an Indonesian independent researcher travelling to the Philippines, Thailand or New Zealand for a conference.
